minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Small Business Assistance Task Force
  Committee Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Tuesday, September 3, 2024
  9:00 AM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  September 3, 2024 / 9:00 AM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Vice Mayor Sharona Nazarian, Councilmember Craig Corman, Assistant
  City Manager Ryan Gohlich, Community Outreach Manager Magdalena
  Davis, Municipal Affairs Program Manager Cindy Owens, Community
  Development Management Analyst Angelina Ramirez, Community
  Development Principal Planner Ray Balderas, Beverly Hills Chamber of
  Commerce President & CEO Todd Johnson, Beverly Hills Chamber of
  Commerce Economic Development Manager Joseph Campbell, Chamber
  Director of Economic & Government Affairs Brittany Ganson, Beverly Hills
  Chamber of Commerce Chairman Bobbe Joy Dawson

  1) Public Comment:
  a. Sherry Andrus: Spoke during Item 5.
  b. Barry Axelrod: Spoke during Item 5

  2) Welcome, Introductions and Purpose of the Task Force:
  a. Barry Axelrod: Beverly Hills Cookies
  b. Shawn Saeedian: Beverly Hills Market
  c. Sherry Andrus: Epiphany Boutique

  3) CA State Legislature Updates for Business:
  a. Presentation by Cindy Owens:
  i. The Property Crime and Retail Theft package of bills were all passed and
  signed by the governor with one exception. The signed bills will all come
  into effect on January 1st, 2025, except for AB 1794. These bills provide a
  variety of new and improved measures to crack down on retail theft.
  ii. The bill to allow for General Law cities such as Beverly Hills to create a city
  attorney’s office to prosecute misdemeanor crimes failed to pass the
  senate.
  iii. SB 1053 passed and is awaiting the governor’s signature. This would
  phase out the thicker plastic bags and would mandate the use of paper
  bags made with 50% post recyclable paper. These bags would be free of
  charge to consumers.
 Highlights for September 3, 2024
Small Business Assistance Task Force Committee

  iv. Proposition 36 aims to classify certain drug offensives as treatment
  mandated felonies and increase the penalties of certain drug crimes.
  v. Proposition 32 would increase the state minimum wage to $18 an hour
  which would then be subject to CPI increases indefinitely.
  b. Governor Newsom is opposed to Proposition 36 and has repeatedly tried to kill it.

  4) Open Air Dining Program Reminders:
  a. Presentation from Angelina Ramirez and Ray Balderas:
  i. The City has been asking business owners to get their applications for the
  permanent OpenBH in since March.
  ii. The City is working proactively with businesses to get their applications in.
  iii. The City has over 60 applications in for either sidewalk dining or for
  parklets. Only 10 applications are for parklets while the rest are for sidewalk
  dining.
  b. The City expects only one more parklet application to be submitted.
  c. The issues that restaurants face of people harassing diners from the sidewalk is
  essentially unstoppable due to first amendment considerations.
  d. Vice Mayor Nazarian believes that the City needs to look into businesses that have
  parklets on T-Zones and see what can be done to mitigate diner harassment.
  e. Previous Meeting Updates:
  i. The Holiday Décor has been updated for the upcoming holiday season.

  5) South Beverly Merchants Discussion:
  a. Sherry Andrus Public Comment: She would like South Beverly to be a “village” that
  offers a diverse dining selection as well as affordable retail for shoppers and
  tourists alike. She wishes to create a South Beverly Merchant Association and has
  been working with other like minded business owners to improve the community
  and to coordinate between businesses and the City
  b. Barry Axelrod Public Comment: He believes that the City will need to get buy in
  from business owners for the Merchant Association to be successful
  c. There were several complaints about eyesores such as plastic bags in the vacant
  properties.
  d. The installation and maintenance of a kiosk was prohibitively expensive due to
  kiosks primarily making money through ad revenue, which the City would heavily
  limit.
  e. The CVB has 2 apps aimed at tourists to promote businesses. Love Beverly Hills
  is run by the CVB and is for restaurant, hotel, and event promotion while the
  Historical Society app is for walking tours of the city.
  f. The Vice Mayor would like South Beverly Merchants to cooperate with the CVB to
  promote their business on the Love Beverly Hills app.
  g. The Liaisons have agreed to make this agenda item a standing item to reappear
  in future meetings.
 Highlights for September 3, 2024
Small Business Assistance Task Force Committee

  6) Information Sharing & Discussion by Small Business Task Force:
  a. When the Chamber wants to start a committee, it just needs approval from the
  Chamber’s board.
  b. The City is looking at improving the façade of the South Beverly parking structure
  as well as their other parking structures.
  c. The white tree wrap lights on South Beverly will remain up year-round.
  d. Next Night will be Saturday September 28th.

  7) Future Agenda Items Discussion:
  a. Todd Johnson would like to discuss A frame signs at the next meeting.

  8) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: September 3, 2024 / 10:08 AM
